verses.text: Jesus answered them with another story:
“Heaven’s Kingdom is like a king who threw a wedding feast for his son.”
“He sent his servants to call the invited guests, but they wouldn’t come.”
“He sent other servants out: ‘Tell the guests, “Dinner’s ready! I’ve prepared the feast, slaughtered my cattle and fattened calves. Come to the wedding!”’”
“But they shrugged it off and went their own way—one to his farm, another to his business.”
“The rest grabbed his servants, treated them horribly, and killed them.”
“The king was furious. He sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.”
“Then he told his servants, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but the invited guests weren’t worthy.”
“‘Go to the street crossings and invite everyone you find to the wedding.’”
“The servants went out into the streets and gathered everyone they found, good and bad. The wedding hall filled up.”
“When the king came in to greet the guests, he spotted someone who wasn’t wearing wedding clothes.”
“He asked him, ‘Friend, how did you get in here without wedding clothes?’ The man had nothing to say.”
“Then the king told his servants, ‘Tie his hands and feet, take him away, and throw him into outer darkness.’ That’s where there’ll be weeping and grinding of teeth.”
“Many are invited, but few are chosen.”
Then the Pharisees met up and plotted how to trap Jesus with his own words.
They sent their disciples along with the Herodians. “Teacher, we know you’re honest and teach God’s way truthfully, no matter who’s listening. You don’t play favorites.”
“So give us your take: is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?”
Jesus knew their bad intentions and said, “Why are you testing me, hypocrites?”
“Show me the tax coin.” They brought him a denarius.
He asked, “Whose face and inscription are on this?”
They answered, “Caesar’s.” Then he said, “Give Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and give God what belongs to God.”
When they heard that, they were amazed. They left him and went away.
That same day, the Sadducees—who say there’s no resurrection—came up and questioned him.
They said, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If a man dies without children, his brother must marry the widow and raise up children for his brother.’”
“There were seven brothers among us. The first married and died without children, leaving his wife to his brother.”
“The same thing happened to the second and third, all the way through the seventh.”
“After them all, the woman died too.”
“So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be? All seven married her.”
Jesus answered, “You’re off track because you don’t know the Scriptures or God’s power.”
“When people rise from the dead, they don’t marry or get married off. They’re like God’s angels in heaven.”
“About the resurrection of the dead, haven’t you read what God told you?”
“‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’ God isn’t the God of the dead; he’s the God of the living.”
When the crowds heard this, they were amazed by his teaching.
When the Pharisees heard Jesus had shut the Sadducees down, they gathered together.
One of them, an expert in the Law, tested Jesus with a question:
“Teacher, which commandment in the Law is the greatest?”
Jesus said, “‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your mind.’”
“That’s the first and greatest commandment.”
“The second is like it: ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’”
“The whole Law and the Prophets hang on these two commandments.”
While the Pharisees were gathered, Jesus asked them a question:
“What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They answered, “David’s.”
He asked, “Then why does David, speaking by the Spirit, call him ‘Lord’?”
“‘The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies beneath your feet.’”
“If David calls him ‘Lord,’ how is he David’s son?”
Nobody could answer him. From that day on, nobody dared ask him another question.
